Dear Sirs,
Sub: Disclosure under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
The Company has received an order dated October 6, 2026 (“Order”) passed by the Joint
Commissioner of Customs (Import), ACC, Mumbai levying on the Company a redemption fine
and penalty aggregating Rs. 18,74,978 under applicable provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
The Order has been passed alleging that the Company discharged a lesser custom duty by
incorrect classification of imported goods in the Bill of Entry. The Company intends to file an
appeal against the Order.
The financial impact of the Order is to the extent of the redemption fine and penalty levied.
There is no impact on operations or other activities of the Company due to the Order.
The Order was received by the Company today, by email, at 12:21 p.m. (IST).

Dear Sir/Madam,
Ref: Disclosure under Regulation 30 and other applicable regulations of the SEBI (Listing
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing
Regulations”)
The Board of Directors of the Bank, at its meeting held today, based on the recommendation of the
Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee (“GNRC”), considered and approved the
re-appointment of Mrs. Lily Vadera (DIN: 09400410) as an Independent Director of the Bank for a
period of 3 (three) years with effect from November 26, 2026 to November 25, 2029 (both days
inclusive), subject to approval of the shareholders of the Bank.
We wish to inform you that Mrs. Vadera is not related to any other Directors or Key Managerial
Personnel of the Bank. Further, she is not debarred from holding the office of a Director, by virtue of
any order passed by SEBI or any other such authority. The aforesaid re-appointment shall be placed
before the shareholders of the Bank for their approval, shortly.
We further inform that Mr. Kaizad Bharucha (DIN: 02490648), Deputy Managing Director, HDFC
Bank has requested cessation from the service of the Bank with effect from the close of business hours
on December 31, 2026.
The GNRC and the Board of Directors, at their respective meetings held on October 16, 2026 and
October 17, 2026, respected the decision of Mr. Bharucha and accepted his request to be forwarded to
the Reserve Bank of India (“RBI”) for approval.
The GNRC and the Board placed on record their sincere appreciation and gratitude for Mr. Kaizad
Bharucha’s outstanding contribution to the Bank over a distinguished association spanning more than
three decades. During this period, Mr. Bharucha played a significant role in the Bank’s growth and
institutional development and made an enduring contribution to the strength and resilience of its
business. The Directors particularly acknowledged that the Bank’s robust credit architecture has been
one of its defining institutional strengths and recognised Mr. Bharucha as one of the principal architects
who helped conceptualise, establish and develop this framework.

Outcome of the Board Meeting held today, i.e., 12 October 2026
Further to the communication dated 07 October 2026, this is to inform that the meeting of the Board of
Directors of the Company (“Board”) was held today, i.e. 12 October 2026, which commenced at 05:00
P.M. and concluded at 05:50 P.M., IST. The Board, inter alia, considered and approved the following:
1. Issuance of Non-Convertible Debentures
The Board of Directors has approved the issuance of listed, rated, unsecured, redeemable non-
convertible debentures ("NCDs"), on a private placement basis, in one or more tranches and/or
series, for an aggregate amount not exceeding INR 10,000 Crore.
The Board has also approved the related issuance framework and authorised the Finance Committee
to determine and approve the tranche-specific terms and conditions of the NCDs, including matters
relating to their issuance, allocation and allotment, within the framework approved by the Board.
The disclosures required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 shall be made at the appropriate stage, upon issuance and/or
allotment of the NCDs.
2. Resignation of Mr. Gautam Doshi
Mr. Gautam Doshi (DIN: 00004612) has tendered his resignation as a Non-Executive, Independent
Director of the Company with effect from 12 October 2026, citing personal reasons. He has
confirmed that there are no material reasons for his resignation other than those stated in his
resignation letter. Consequent upon his resignation, he has also ceased to hold positions on the
Committees of the Board of Directors of the Company.
The Board of Directors has taken note of the resignation of Mr. Gautam Doshi and placed on record
its sincere appreciation for the valuable guidance and contributions made by him during his tenure
as an Independent Director of the Company.
The details required under Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 are provided in Annexure A and the resignation
letter of Mr. Gautam Doshi is enclosed herewith as Annexure B.

Sub: Disclosure under Regulation(s) 30 read with 51 of the Securities and Exchange
Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
This is further to our disclosure dated July 22, 2026 in connection with material tax litigation
reported in the Integrated Filing (Governance) of Tata Steel Limited (‘Company’) for quarter
ended June 30, 2026.
Background:
The Company, through its earlier disclosures, had informed that the relevant income tax
authorities have disallowed the Company’s claims of deduction for interest expenditure under
Section 36(1)(iii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, in respect of loans borrowed and utilized by the
Company for acquisition of Corus Group Plc, foreign subsidiary, for the period FY2008 through
FY2015. The aggregate tax exposure arising from this issue for the entire period is ~₹1,901
crore. The Company had, from time to time, filed appeal against these orders of the income tax
authorities before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (‘Authority’).
Case of FY2008
After several hearings, on February 27, 2026, the Company received a favourable order dated
February 20, 2026 from the Authority for FY2008 (‘Order 1’) wherein the claim of deduction for
interest expenditure was allowed. The tax exposure for FY2008 is ~₹215 crore. Accordingly, the
tax exposure against the Company will get reduce from ~₹1,901 crore to ~₹1,686 crore once
the Assessing Officer will give effect to this Order 1 through a consequential separate order. The
Company has made necessary disclosures in this regard to the stock exchanges on
February 28, 2026.
Case of FY2009
For the period FY2009, the Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Circle 2(3)(1), Mumbai vide
his order dated January 10, 2014 had disallowed the claim of ₹813.65 crore towards deduction
for interest expenditure under Section 36(1)(iii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. On
February 4, 2014, the Company had filed an appeal against the order before the Authority. The
matter was heard over multiple hearings.
Present Status:
The final hearing in the matter of FY2009 took place before the Authority in June 2026. The
Company, on September 28, 2026, received a favourable order dated September 18, 2026
(‘Order 2’) from the Authority wherein the claim of deduction for interest expenditure was allowed
following the earlier Order 1 for FY2008. The tax exposure for FY2009 is ~₹427 crore.
Accordingly, the tax exposure against the Company will get reduced from ~₹1,686 crore to
~₹1,259 crore once the Assessing Officer will give effect to this Order 2 through a consequential
separate order. Subsequently, the Company will make necessary adjustments in its contingent
liability reported in notes to its Financial Statements.
The Company believes that these Orders passed by the Authority will have persuasive impact
on co-related pending litigations on the same issue for the period FY2010 to FY2015 as
mentioned above.
This disclosure is being made by the Company in compliance with Regulations 30 and 51 of the
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)
Regulations, 2015, as amended.
